text:
Runbook RB-ACC-01: Account locked after failed sign-ins (Account lockout and access requests).
Applies when: User is locked out after too many wrong password attempts.
People often describe this as: account is locked; locked out after wrong password; too many failed attempts; locked out of my laptop login; account disabled after sign-in attempts; please unlock my account.
Check first: Lockout is not flagged by Security; No other lockouts in the last 24 hours.
title: Account locked after failed sign-ins

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-01: Account locked after failed sign-ins (Account lockout and access requests).
Steps:
1. Check whether an old saved password on a phone, mail app or other device keeps retrying
2. Wait for the automatic lockout to expire, or let the user use self-service reset to clear it
3. Unlock the account if the policy allows
4. Ask the user to sign in on one device only
5. Confirm access works
title: Account locked after failed sign-ins

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-01: Account locked after failed sign-ins (Account lockout and access requests).
Escalate to a human if: Lockout repeats within 24 hours or from an unfamiliar location, which can mean an attack; Account is flagged by Security; Sign-in attempts came from unknown locations; Several users are locked out at the same time.
title: Account locked after failed sign-ins

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-02: Shared mailbox or group access (Account lockout and access requests).
Applies when: User needs access to a shared mailbox, distribution list or team group.
People often describe this as: need access to a shared mailbox; add me to the team group; cannot see the shared inbox; join the distribution list; access to our team mailbox; added to a group but it is not showing.
Check first: Exact group or mailbox name is known; Business reason is stated.
title: Shared mailbox or group access

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-02: Shared mailbox or group access (Account lockout and access requests).
Steps:
1. Confirm the exact group or mailbox name
2. Confirm the business need
3. Send an approval request to the resource owner
4. After approval, tell the user it can take up to 60 minutes, then to fully close and reopen Outlook
5. If access was given through a group, the mailbox may need to be added manually, or opened in Outlook on the web
title: Shared mailbox or group access

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-02: Shared mailbox or group access (Account lockout and access requests).
Escalate to a human if: Group holds finance, HR or restricted data; Approver does not respond within 2 working days; Name does not match any known group; Mailbox still does not open after the propagation window.
title: Shared mailbox or group access

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-03: New joiner access setup (Account lockout and access requests).
Applies when: New employee cannot reach standard tools on or after the first day.
People often describe this as: just started; new joiner; first week at the company; joined recently; account was not ready when I arrived; cannot reach any of the standard tools; nothing set up for me on my first day.
Check first: Employee record exists; Start date has passed.
title: New joiner access setup

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-03: New joiner access setup (Account lockout and access requests).
Steps:
1. Confirm the employee record and role
2. Request the standard role access bundle
3. Ask the user to sign in and check each core tool
4. Confirm completion
title: New joiner access setup

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-03: New joiner access setup (Account lockout and access requests).
Escalate to a human if: No employee record found; Role needs non-standard access.
title: New joiner access setup

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-04: Business application access request (Account lockout and access requests).
Applies when: User needs access to an internal business application.
People often describe this as: need access to an application; please give me access to the app; request access to a business system; add me as a user; new access request for a tool; want permission to use a system.
Check first: Application name is known; Application is in the access catalog.
title: Business application access request

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-04: Business application access request (Account lockout and access requests).
Steps:
1. Identify the application and role requested
2. Confirm it is in the access catalog
3. Send an approval request to the manager
4. Tell the user to expect access within one working day after approval
title: Business application access request

text:
Runbook RB-ACC-04: Business application access request (Account lockout and access requests).
Escalate to a human if: Application is not in the catalog; Requested role is privileged or admin; Manager is unknown.
title: Business application access request

text:
Runbook RB-APP-01: Internal application login error (Internal application errors).
Applies when: User cannot sign in to an internal business application.
People often describe this as: cannot log in to the app; internal tool login fails; login keeps failing on our system; stuck on the login screen; single sign on error in the application; app says invalid credentials.
Check first: Correct address is used; Account is active.
title: Internal application login error

text:
Runbook RB-APP-01: Internal application login error (Internal application errors).
Steps:
1. Confirm the application address
2. Check the application status
3. Sign in using single sign-on
4. Clear browser cache or try another browser
title: Internal application login error

text:
Runbook RB-APP-01: Internal application login error (Internal application errors).
Escalate to a human if: Message says access denied or role missing; Application is down for all users.
title: Internal application login error

text:
Runbook RB-APP-02: Application slow or timing out (Internal application errors).
Applies when: Internal application is slow or requests time out.
People often describe this as: application is slow; app keeps timing out; system hangs when saving; screen freezes then an error; internal system very slow; page takes forever to load in the tool.
Check first: Time and action that was slow are known.
title: Application slow or timing out

text:
Runbook RB-APP-02: Application slow or timing out (Internal application errors).
Steps:
1. Check the application status
2. Ask the user to note the time and screen
3. Clear the browser cache and retry
4. Retry outside peak hours
title: Application slow or timing out

text:
Runbook RB-APP-02: Application slow or timing out (Internal application errors).
Escalate to a human if: Several users report the same slowness; Error message mentions a server or database.
title: Application slow or timing out

text:
Runbook RB-APP-03: Report or export fails (Internal application errors).
Applies when: Report fails to run or export to Excel or PDF fails.
People often describe this as: report will not run; export to excel fails; download of the report fails; cannot export to pdf; report errors out; data export stuck.
Check first: Report name and filters are known.
title: Report or export fails

text:
Runbook RB-APP-03: Report or export fails (Internal application errors).
Steps:
1. Reduce the date range or filters
2. Try another export format
3. Retry once after a few minutes
4. Capture the error message and time
title: Report or export fails

text:
Runbook RB-APP-03: Report or export fails (Internal application errors).
Escalate to a human if: Error repeats with small filters; Report data looks wrong or incomplete.
title: Report or export fails

text:
Runbook RB-COL-01: Audio or video not working in meetings (Collaboration tools).
Applies when: Microphone, speaker or camera does not work in Teams or similar tools.
People often describe this as: mic not working in teams; camera not working in a meeting; no sound in the call; others cannot hear me; webcam shows a black screen; audio cutting out on calls.
Check first: Headset or camera is plugged in; Other apps are not using the camera.
title: Audio or video not working in meetings

text:
Runbook RB-COL-01: Audio or video not working in meetings (Collaboration tools).
Steps:
1. Open Teams Settings > Devices and choose the correct microphone, speaker and camera
2. Run Make a test call
3. Check the operating system privacy settings allow Teams to use the microphone and camera
4. Close other apps that use the camera or microphone
5. Unplug and reconnect external devices, and charge Bluetooth devices and disconnect them from other devices
6. Restart the meeting app or the device
title: Audio or video not working in meetings

text:
Runbook RB-COL-01: Audio or video not working in meetings (Collaboration tools).
Escalate to a human if: Device is not detected by the operating system; Problem continues with different headsets; User is on a virtual desktop (VDI).
title: Audio or video not working in meetings

text:
Runbook RB-COL-02: Cannot join a meeting (Collaboration tools).
Applies when: User cannot join a scheduled online meeting.
People often describe this as: cannot join the meeting; meeting link not working; stuck at joining; error when joining a teams call; join button does nothing; cannot enter the video call.
Check first: Meeting link is available.
title: Cannot join a meeting

text:
Runbook RB-COL-02: Cannot join a meeting (Collaboration tools).
Steps:
1. Check the link and the meeting time
2. Sign in with the work account
3. Try the web version
4. Update the meeting app
title: Cannot join a meeting

text:
Runbook RB-COL-02: Cannot join a meeting (Collaboration tools).
Escalate to a human if: Meeting is hosted by an external organization with restrictions; Error mentions a policy block; Several participants cannot join the same meeting.
title: Cannot join a meeting

text:
Runbook RB-COL-03: Collaboration app sign-in loop (Collaboration tools).
Applies when: App keeps asking for sign-in or shows a repeating error.
People often describe this as: teams keeps asking me to sign in; sign in loop; app asks for login again and again; cannot stay signed in to teams; login screen keeps coming back; collaboration app will not let me in.
Check first: Password is current; Internet works.
title: Collaboration app sign-in loop

text:
Runbook RB-COL-03: Collaboration app sign-in loop (Collaboration tools).
Steps:
1. Sign out completely
2. Clear the application cache
3. Sign in again with the work account
4. Restart the device
title: Collaboration app sign-in loop

text:
Runbook RB-COL-03: Collaboration app sign-in loop (Collaboration tools).
Escalate to a human if: Error mentions conditional access or device compliance; Problem continues after clearing the cache; Several users see the same sign-in error.
title: Collaboration app sign-in loop

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-01: Shared drive not showing (Shared drives and file access).
Applies when: Mapped drive is missing or disconnected.
People often describe this as: shared drive missing; mapped drive disappeared; cannot see the network drive; drive not showing in explorer; z drive is gone; lost connection to the shared folder drive.
Check first: User is on the office network or VPN.
title: Shared drive not showing

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-01: Shared drive not showing (Shared drives and file access).
Steps:
1. Confirm the VPN or office network is connected
2. Remap the drive using the correct path
3. Sign in again if prompted
4. Restart the laptop
title: Shared drive not showing

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-01: Shared drive not showing (Shared drives and file access).
Escalate to a human if: Path is reported as not found; Many users cannot reach the drive.
title: Shared drive not showing

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-02: Permission denied on a folder (Shared drives and file access).
Applies when: User sees access denied on a shared folder.
People often describe this as: access denied to a folder; permission denied on the shared folder; cannot open the folder, no permission; need access to a folder; not authorized to open the directory; you do not have permission message.
Check first: Folder path is known; Business reason is stated.
title: Permission denied on a folder

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-02: Permission denied on a folder (Shared drives and file access).
Steps:
1. Confirm the exact folder path and owner
2. Send an approval request to the folder owner
3. After approval, wait 30 minutes
4. Ask the user to sign out and in
title: Permission denied on a folder

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-02: Permission denied on a folder (Shared drives and file access).
Escalate to a human if: Folder holds confidential or restricted data; Owner cannot be identified; Approval is not given within 2 working days.
title: Permission denied on a folder

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-03: Restore a deleted or overwritten file (Shared drives and file access).
Applies when: User deleted or overwrote a file by mistake.
People often describe this as: deleted a file by mistake; overwrote my document; need an older version of a file; recover a deleted file; file disappeared from the shared folder; restore a previous version.
Check first: File name and last location are known.
title: Restore a deleted or overwritten file

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-03: Restore a deleted or overwritten file (Shared drives and file access).
Steps:
1. Check the local Recycle Bin
2. For OneDrive or SharePoint files, check the web recycle bin, including the second-stage bin
3. Use version history in OneDrive or SharePoint, or Previous Versions if backups are turned on
4. Ask when the file was last seen
title: Restore a deleted or overwritten file

text:
Runbook RB-DRV-03: Restore a deleted or overwritten file (Shared drives and file access).
Escalate to a human if: File is not found in any bin or version history; Deletion was longer ago than the retention period; A whole-folder or whole-drive restore is needed.
title: Restore a deleted or overwritten file

text:
Runbook RB-EML-01: Outlook not syncing (Email and calendar).
Applies when: Outlook shows disconnected, offline or old mail.
People often describe this as: outlook not syncing; outlook shows disconnected; emails not updating; outlook says working offline; new mail not coming in; outlook stuck loading.
Check first: Internet works; Account password is current.
title: Outlook not syncing

text:
Runbook RB-EML-01: Outlook not syncing (Email and calendar).
Steps:
1. Check the Send/Receive tab: if Work Offline is highlighted, click it once
2. Check whether Outlook on the web works, to tell a client problem from a service problem
3. Check the email service status
4. Restart Outlook
5. Check whether a firewall, antivirus or add-in is interfering
6. Sign out and sign in again
7. Create a new Outlook profile as the last step
title: Outlook not syncing

text:
Runbook RB-EML-01: Outlook not syncing (Email and calendar).
Escalate to a human if: Webmail also fails; Problem remains after a new profile; Email service shows an outage.
title: Outlook not syncing

text:
Runbook RB-EML-02: Mailbox full (Email and calendar).
Applies when: User cannot send or receive because the mailbox is full.
People often describe this as: mailbox is full; storage full cannot send email; mailbox quota exceeded; inbox over its limit; cannot receive mail, no space; need to clear mailbox space.
Check first: User mailbox size is near its limit.
title: Mailbox full

text:
Runbook RB-EML-02: Mailbox full (Email and calendar).
Steps:
1. Use Mailbox Cleanup to view mailbox and folder sizes
2. Empty Deleted Items and Junk Email
3. Delete large attachments from Sent Items, then empty Deleted Items again
4. Archive older items if the archive feature is turned on
5. Confirm new mail is arriving
title: Mailbox full

text:
Runbook RB-EML-02: Mailbox full (Email and calendar).
Escalate to a human if: User asks for a larger quota; Mailbox still full after cleanup, since hidden or retained items can still count toward the quota.
title: Mailbox full

text:
Runbook RB-EML-03: Calendar invites missing or not updating (Email and calendar).
Applies when: Meeting invites do not show or updates are missing.
People often describe this as: meeting invite not showing; calendar not updating; invites missing from my calendar; accepted meeting does not appear; calendar out of sync; cannot see meetings I was invited to.
Check first: Correct calendar is selected; Mailbox is syncing.
title: Calendar invites missing or not updating

text:
Runbook RB-EML-03: Calendar invites missing or not updating (Email and calendar).
Steps:
1. Check the right calendar and view are selected
2. Force a sync
3. Check the junk and other folders for invites
4. Check whether a delegate has accepted the invite
title: Calendar invites missing or not updating

text:
Runbook RB-EML-03: Calendar invites missing or not updating (Email and calendar).
Escalate to a human if: Invite from an external organization never arrives; Calendar items disappear repeatedly.
title: Calendar invites missing or not updating

text:
Runbook RB-EML-04: Email bounced or not delivered (Email and calendar).
Applies when: Sent email returns an error or the recipient does not receive it.
People often describe this as: email bounced back; message not delivered; undeliverable email; delivery failed error; sent mail returned with an error; recipient did not get my email.
Check first: Bounce message or recipient address is available.
title: Email bounced or not delivered

text:
Runbook RB-EML-04: Email bounced or not delivered (Email and calendar).
Steps:
1. Read the User information section of the bounce message and note the error code
2. 5.1.1: the address does not exist, so check spelling and confirm with the recipient
3. 5.2.2: the recipient mailbox is full, so try later or tell the recipient
4. Message too large: reduce the attachment or share a link instead
5. 5.7.x: delivery blocked by policy or permissions, so escalate
title: Email bounced or not delivered

text:
Runbook RB-EML-04: Email bounced or not delivered (Email and calendar).
Escalate to a human if: Bounce mentions a security or policy block; External domain is blocked; Bounce repeats after correcting the address.
title: Email bounced or not delivered

text:
Runbook RB-HW-01: Laptop running slowly (Laptop hardware).
Applies when: Laptop is slow, freezing or has long start-up time.
People often describe this as: laptop is slow; computer freezing; machine takes forever to start; laptop running slowly; everything is sluggish on my pc; laptop hangs when I open files.
Check first: Laptop has not been restarted recently; Disk space is known.
title: Laptop running slowly

text:
Runbook RB-HW-01: Laptop running slowly (Laptop hardware).
Steps:
1. Restart the laptop
2. Close unused applications and browser tabs
3. Check free disk space
4. Install pending updates
title: Laptop running slowly

text:
Runbook RB-HW-01: Laptop running slowly (Laptop hardware).
Escalate to a human if: Slowness continues after all steps; Disk or memory errors are shown.
title: Laptop running slowly

text:
Runbook RB-HW-02: Battery or charger problem (Laptop hardware).
Applies when: Laptop does not charge or battery drains quickly.
People often describe this as: laptop not charging; battery drains fast; charger not working; battery dies quickly; laptop will not hold a charge; charging light does not come on.
Check first: Charger is the correct model; Wall outlet works.
title: Battery or charger problem

text:
Runbook RB-HW-02: Battery or charger problem (Laptop hardware).
Steps:
1. Try another outlet and cable
2. Reseat the charger and check the port for debris
3. Run the built-in battery diagnostic
4. If the case or touchpad is bulging, stop using the laptop, unplug the charger and do not press on the battery
5. Do not remove or dispose of a swollen battery yourself, and request a replacement
title: Battery or charger problem

text:
Runbook RB-HW-02: Battery or charger problem (Laptop hardware).
Escalate to a human if: Battery is swollen, hot or smells burnt, stop using and escalate at once; Diagnostic reports a failing battery; Charger or port is visibly damaged.
title: Battery or charger problem

text:
Runbook RB-HW-03: Screen, keyboard or physical damage (Laptop hardware).
Applies when: Laptop has a cracked screen, broken keys or other physical damage.
People often describe this as: cracked screen; broken keyboard; laptop damaged; dropped my laptop; keys not working; screen broken or flickering; liquid spilled on the laptop.
Check first: Asset tag is known.
title: Screen, keyboard or physical damage

text:
Runbook RB-HW-03: Screen, keyboard or physical damage (Laptop hardware).
Steps:
1. Collect the asset tag and a short description of the damage
2. Advise the user to back up files if the device still works
3. Open a hardware repair request
4. Route to the Hardware team
title: Screen, keyboard or physical damage

text:
Runbook RB-HW-03: Screen, keyboard or physical damage (Laptop hardware).
Escalate to a human if: Always needs a human decision on repair or replacement.
This kind of problem is never resolved automatically. A human always handles it.
title: Screen, keyboard or physical damage

text:
Runbook RB-NET-01: Wi-Fi will not connect (Wi-Fi and network).
Applies when: Laptop cannot join the office Wi-Fi.
People often describe this as: wifi not connecting; cannot join the office wifi; laptop will not connect to wifi; wifi shows no network; wireless not working; cannot find the corporate wifi.
Check first: Other devices connect to the same Wi-Fi; Wi-Fi is turned on.
title: Wi-Fi will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-NET-01: Wi-Fi will not connect (Wi-Fi and network).
Steps:
1. Check Wi-Fi is on and Airplane mode is off
2. Forget the network and join it again
3. Check whether another device connects to the same network
4. If both bands are listed, try the other Wi-Fi band
5. Restart the laptop and check for updates
6. Use network reset only as the last step
title: Wi-Fi will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-NET-01: Wi-Fi will not connect (Wi-Fi and network).
Escalate to a human if: Only this device fails after all steps; Many users in the same area report the problem.
title: Wi-Fi will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-NET-02: No internet on wired connection (Wi-Fi and network).
Applies when: Desk or dock connection shows no network.
People often describe this as: no internet on cable; ethernet not working; docking station has no network; wired connection shows no internet; network cable plugged in but nothing; desk network port not working.
Check first: Cable is plugged in at both ends.
title: No internet on wired connection

text:
Runbook RB-NET-02: No internet on wired connection (Wi-Fi and network).
Steps:
1. Reseat the network cable and dock
2. Try a different wall port or cable
3. Run the Windows network troubleshooter
4. Disable and enable the network adapter
5. Restart the laptop
title: No internet on wired connection

text:
Runbook RB-NET-02: No internet on wired connection (Wi-Fi and network).
Escalate to a human if: Wall port appears dead; Several desks on the same floor are affected.
title: No internet on wired connection

text:
Runbook RB-NET-03: Slow network (Wi-Fi and network).
Applies when: User reports slow browsing or downloads.
People often describe this as: internet very slow; network is crawling; pages load slowly; downloads are slow; everything lags on the network; slow connection today.
Check first: User can reach websites at all.
title: Slow network

text:
Runbook RB-NET-03: Slow network (Wi-Fi and network).
Steps:
1. Run a speed test and note the result
2. Close heavy downloads and streams
3. Try a wired connection
4. Check the network status page
title: Slow network

text:
Runbook RB-NET-03: Slow network (Wi-Fi and network).
Escalate to a human if: Slowness continues for more than a day; Many users report slowness.
title: Slow network

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-01: Cannot print (Printers and peripherals).
Applies when: Print jobs do not print or stay in the queue.
People often describe this as: cannot print; print job stuck in the queue; printer not printing; documents will not print; printer shows offline; nothing comes out of the printer.
Check first: Printer is switched on; Paper and toner are available.
title: Cannot print

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-01: Cannot print (Printers and peripherals).
Steps:
1. Run the printer troubleshooter
2. Check the printer is not set to Use Printer Offline or Pause Printing
3. Cancel stuck jobs in the print queue
4. Restart the print spooler if cancelling does not clear the queue
5. Turn the printer off for 60 seconds and restart the PC
6. Print a test page
title: Cannot print

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-01: Cannot print (Printers and peripherals).
Escalate to a human if: Printer is offline for all users; Driver error continues after the steps; User cannot restart the spooler on a managed device.
title: Cannot print

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-02: Add a printer (Printers and peripherals).
Applies when: User needs a printer added to their laptop.
People often describe this as: add a printer; printer not in my list; set up the floor printer; need the printer installed on my laptop; map the network printer; cannot find the printer to add.
Check first: Printer name or location is known; Device is on the office network.
title: Add a printer

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-02: Add a printer (Printers and peripherals).
Steps:
1. Find the printer name or location
2. Add it from the self-service printer list
3. Set it as default if requested
4. Print a test page
title: Add a printer

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-02: Add a printer (Printers and peripherals).
Escalate to a human if: Printer is not in the list; Driver install fails.
title: Add a printer

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-03: Scan to email not working (Printers and peripherals).
Applies when: Scanner does not send documents to email.
People often describe this as: scan to email not working; scanner not sending documents; scanned document never arrives; scan to folder failing; copier will not email scans; scanner emails are missing.
Check first: Scan destination address is known.
title: Scan to email not working

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-03: Scan to email not working (Printers and peripherals).
Steps:
1. Check the destination email address on the scanner
2. Check the user's mailbox and junk folder
3. Retry with a smaller document
4. Try scan to folder as an alternative
title: Scan to email not working

text:
Runbook RB-PRT-03: Scan to email not working (Printers and peripherals).
Escalate to a human if: Scanner shows a network or server error; Several users have the same problem.
title: Scan to email not working

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-01: Forgotten password (Password and MFA).
Applies when: User forgot their password and cannot sign in.
People often describe this as: forgot my password; cannot remember my password; do not remember my login password; need a password reset link; password not working, need a new one; reset my password.
Check first: Account is not locked; Account is not an admin or privileged account; User has access to their recovery email or phone; Self-service reset is enabled by the organization and the user has registered recovery details.
title: Forgotten password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-01: Forgotten password (Password and MFA).
Steps:
1. Direct the user to the self-service password reset page
2. Send a reset link to the registered recovery address
3. Ask the user to choose a new password that meets policy
4. Ask the user to sign in and confirm it works
title: Forgotten password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-01: Forgotten password (Password and MFA).
Escalate to a human if: User cannot access the recovery email or phone; Reset link fails twice; Ticket mentions an admin or privileged account; Reset page says the account is not enabled for self-service reset or is not registered; Password is managed on-premises and cannot be reset online.
title: Forgotten password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-02: Expired password (Password and MFA).
Applies when: Sign-in shows that the password has expired.
People often describe this as: password expired; system says I must change my password; told to update my password; password change required at login; password has run out; password is due for renewal.
Check first: User is on the office network or VPN; Account is not locked.
title: Expired password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-02: Expired password (Password and MFA).
Steps:
1. Open the self-service password change page
2. Set a new password that meets policy
3. Update the saved password on phone and mail apps
4. Sign out and sign in again
title: Expired password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-02: Expired password (Password and MFA).
Escalate to a human if: Change is rejected even though the password meets policy; Account locks again after the change.
title: Expired password

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-03: MFA code not arriving (Password and MFA).
Applies when: User does not receive the MFA text or call.
People often describe this as: did not get the verification code; text message code not coming; authenticator code not received; no sms for login; waiting for the one time passcode; code never arrives on my phone.
Check first: Phone has signal; Registered phone number is correct; Phone date and time are set to automatic.
title: MFA code not arriving

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-03: MFA code not arriving (Password and MFA).
Steps:
1. Wait 60 seconds and request one new code only, because repeated requests can cause a temporary block
2. Check the phone is not blocking texts from unknown numbers
3. Switch to another registered method such as the authenticator app or a code in a signed-in mail app
4. Retry sign-in
title: MFA code not arriving

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-03: MFA code not arriving (Password and MFA).
Escalate to a human if: No registered method works, an admin must require MFA re-registration; Registered phone number is wrong or outdated; Several users do not receive codes at the same time.
title: MFA code not arriving

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-04: MFA device lost or replaced (Password and MFA).
Applies when: User has a new phone or lost the old one and cannot approve MFA.
People often describe this as: got a new phone and cannot approve login; lost my phone with the authenticator app; changed my phone number; old phone was reset, now stuck at approval; authenticator app needs to move to a new device; cannot approve the sign-in prompt anymore.
Check first: User can describe the old device; Backup method is checked.
title: MFA device lost or replaced

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-04: MFA device lost or replaced (Password and MFA).
Steps:
1. Ask whether another registered method works or Authenticator cloud backup was turned on before the old phone was wiped
2. Explain that the help desk or an admin must clear the MFA methods after verifying identity
3. Explain that all old methods are removed and new ones are registered at the next sign-in
4. Route the ticket to the Identity team for verified re-registration
title: MFA device lost or replaced

text:
Runbook RB-PWD-04: MFA device lost or replaced (Password and MFA).
Escalate to a human if: Always requires identity verification by a human; User asks for a reset without verification.
This kind of problem is never resolved automatically. A human always handles it.
title: MFA device lost or replaced

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-01: Suspected phishing email (Security reports).
Applies when: User received or clicked a suspicious email.
People often describe this as: suspicious email; phishing email; clicked a link in a strange email; email asking for my password; fake message pretending to be hr; entered my password on a strange site.
Check first: Do not open links or attachments.
title: Suspected phishing email

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-01: Suspected phishing email (Security reports).
Steps:
1. Tell the user not to click, reply or forward the email
2. Ask the user to use the report phishing button
3. If a link was clicked, advise disconnecting the device from the network and entering no more information
4. Collect the sender, the time, the link and anything entered
5. Route to Security immediately, and mark as urgent if credentials were entered
title: Suspected phishing email

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-01: Suspected phishing email (Security reports).
Escalate to a human if: Always escalate to Security; User clicked a link or entered credentials.
This kind of problem is never resolved automatically. A human always handles it.
title: Suspected phishing email

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-02: Lost or stolen device (Security reports).
Applies when: User reports a lost or stolen laptop or phone.
People often describe this as: lost my laptop; laptop stolen; cannot find my company laptop; left my phone in a taxi; device is missing; someone took my work laptop.
Check first: Asset tag or device type is known.
title: Lost or stolen device

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-02: Lost or stolen device (Security reports).
Steps:
1. Collect when and where the device was lost and whether it was encrypted and enrolled in management
2. Tell the user to report now and not to search everywhere first
3. Advise reporting to the police if theft is suspected and keeping the report number
4. Route to Security immediately for remote lock or wipe
title: Lost or stolen device

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-02: Lost or stolen device (Security reports).
Escalate to a human if: Always escalate to Security; Device holds company data.
This kind of problem is never resolved automatically. A human always handles it.
title: Lost or stolen device

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-03: Suspicious account activity (Security reports).
Applies when: User sees unexpected sign-in alerts or MFA prompts they did not start.
People often describe this as: unexpected sign in alert; login prompts I did not start; mfa prompts keep coming; someone may be using my account; strange login notification; approval requests I never made.
Check first: Do not approve unknown prompts.
title: Suspicious account activity

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-03: Suspicious account activity (Security reports).
Steps:
1. Tell the user to deny any MFA prompt they did not start, and to use Report as fraud if offered
2. Tell the user not to share any codes
3. If the user already approved a prompt, treat it as urgent
4. Route to Security immediately
5. Password changes should follow Security's instruction
title: Suspicious account activity

text:
Runbook RB-SEC-03: Suspicious account activity (Security reports).
Escalate to a human if: Always escalate to Security; Prompts continue after denial.
This kind of problem is never resolved automatically. A human always handles it.
title: Suspicious account activity

Runbook RB-SFT-01: Install approved software (Software install and licenses).
Applies when: User asks for software on the approved list.
People often describe this as: need software installed; please install an application; install a program on my laptop; want a tool from the approved list; software request; need an app on my machine.
Check first: Software is in the approved catalog; Device is company managed.
title: Install approved software

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-01: Install approved software (Software install and licenses).
Steps:
1. Confirm the software is in the approved catalog
2. Push the package to the device
3. Ask the user to restart if prompted
4. Confirm the software opens
title: Install approved software

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-01: Install approved software (Software install and licenses).
Escalate to a human if: Software is not in the catalog; A paid license is needed and none is free; Install fails twice.
title: Install approved software

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-02: Software license will not activate (Software install and licenses).
Applies when: Application shows an unlicensed or activation error.
People often describe this as: unlicensed product; license not activated; software says not licensed; activation error; license key not working; office shows an unlicensed banner.
Check first: A license that includes the desktop apps is assigned to the user; User signs in with the work account, not a personal one.
title: Software license will not activate

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-02: Software license will not activate (Software install and licenses).
Steps:
1. Confirm the license is assigned to the user
2. Ask the user to sign out of the app and sign in again with the work account
3. If a license is already assigned, an admin can remove and re-add it
4. Check the user has not reached the device limit and remove unused devices
5. Run the built-in activation troubleshooter
title: Software license will not activate

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-02: Software license will not activate (Software install and licenses).
Escalate to a human if: No license is available; Activation still fails after sign-in and license re-assignment.
title: Software license will not activate

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-03: Software update fails (Software install and licenses).
Applies when: Operating system or application update fails or loops.
People often describe this as: update failed; windows update stuck; update keeps restarting; software update will not finish; stuck on updating; update error loop.
Check first: Device is connected to power and the internet; Enough free disk space (Microsoft lists about 20 GB free for a 64-bit upgrade).
title: Software update fails

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-03: Software update fails (Software install and licenses).
Steps:
1. Restart the device and check for updates again
2. Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
3. Disconnect unneeded external devices and docks
4. Check the date and time are set automatically
5. Free disk space if low
6. Retry the update
title: Software update fails

text:
Runbook RB-SFT-03: Software update fails (Software install and licenses).
Escalate to a human if: Update fails three times; Disk space cannot be freed; Device cannot boot normally; Error code points to a driver conflict.
title: Software update fails

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-01: VPN will not connect (VPN and remote access).
Applies when: User cannot connect to the corporate VPN but the internet works.
People often describe this as: vpn not connecting; cannot connect to the vpn; vpn fails when I try to connect; secure connection fails; stuck on connecting; cannot reach internal systems from home.
Check first: Internet works; VPN client is installed; Account is not locked.
title: VPN will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-01: VPN will not connect (VPN and remote access).
Steps:
1. Check the VPN service status
2. Restart the VPN client
3. Clear the cached profile and sign in again
4. Check that a firewall or antivirus is not blocking the VPN client
5. Approve the MFA prompt
6. Test on a different network such as a phone hotspot
title: VPN will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-01: VPN will not connect (VPN and remote access).
Escalate to a human if: Error persists after all steps; Service status shows an outage; Several users report the same problem.
When escalating, when escalating, include when the problem started, whether others are affected, the steps already tried, and the exact error text or a screenshot.
title: VPN will not connect

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-02: VPN slow or disconnecting (VPN and remote access).
Applies when: VPN connects but is slow or drops repeatedly.
People often describe this as: vpn keeps dropping; vpn disconnects every few minutes; vpn is very slow; connection drops while on the vpn; vpn lags; keeps getting kicked off the vpn.
Check first: User is working remotely; Other internet use works.
title: VPN slow or disconnecting

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-02: VPN slow or disconnecting (VPN and remote access).
Steps:
1. Check local internet speed
2. Move closer to the router or use a wired connection
3. Close heavy downloads and video streams
4. Reconnect to a different VPN gateway
title: VPN slow or disconnecting

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-02: VPN slow or disconnecting (VPN and remote access).
Escalate to a human if: Problem persists on more than one network; Several users report drops at the same time.
When escalating, when escalating, include when the problem started, whether others are affected, the steps already tried, and the exact error text or a screenshot.
title: VPN slow or disconnecting

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-03: VPN certificate or profile error (VPN and remote access).
Applies when: VPN shows a certificate, profile or trust error.
People often describe this as: vpn trust error; certificate error when connecting; vpn profile is broken; not trusted warning on the vpn; profile missing or corrupt; security certificate problem on connection.
Check first: Device date and time are correct; Device is company managed.
title: VPN certificate or profile error

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-03: VPN certificate or profile error (VPN and remote access).
Steps:
1. Check the device date, time and time zone
2. Remove the old VPN profile
3. Download a fresh profile from the self-service portal
4. Restart the device and reconnect
title: VPN certificate or profile error

text:
Runbook RB-VPN-03: VPN certificate or profile error (VPN and remote access).
Escalate to a human if: Device is not enrolled in management; Certificate error affects many users.
When escalating, when escalating, include when the problem started, whether others are affected, the steps already tried, and the exact error text or a screenshot.
title: VPN certificate or profile error

text:

Applies when: User needs the VPN client installed or updated.
People often describe this as: need the vpn client; vpn app asks me to update; install the vpn software; vpn client missing on my laptop; vpn update will not install; vpn application needs a new version.

text:

Steps:
